name: Snap
description: Snap is a classic children's card game that tests mental reaction speed and pattern recognition. Players take turns flipping cards from their personal piles onto a central pile or their own discard pile. When two cards of the same rank (e.g., two 7s) appear consecutively or simultaneously on top of piles, the first player to shout 'Snap!' wins the cards. The goal is to win the entire deck.

history.origins: Dates back to the Victorian era (1866 recorded rules). Originally called 'Wait a Minute' or similar names.
timeline: Present: A ubiquitous starter game for toddlers.
history.cultural: The word 'Snap' is synonymous with 'Match' in British English due to this game.
history.evolution: The 'Snap Pot' rule (where ties put cards in center) adds tension.

setup.players: Two to four players typically; the game can be played by up to about six, beyond which it becomes unwieldy. Each player keeps their cards in a face-down stack in front of them.
setup.deck: A standard 52-card pack is used. Suits do not matter; only the ranks (A, 2–10, J, Q, K) matter for matching. Some play with special Snap or matching-card packs.
setup.dealing: Deal entirely to players face-down into personal piles.

rules.objective: Be the last player with cards by calling Snap when two face-up pile tops match in rank; the first to call wins those piles and adds them to the bottom of their face-down pile.
rules.gameplay: The deck is shuffled and dealt out equally to players face-down; players do not look at their cards. Player to dealer's left begins; turn passes clockwise. On your turn you turn the top card of your face-down pile and place it face-up alongside, forming a face-up pile beside your face-down pile. When two face-up pile tops match in rank (e.g. two sixes), any player who notices may shout Snap; the first to do so takes both matching face-up piles and adds them face-down to the bottom of their face-down pile. Play continues from the player to the left of whoever turned. If you have no face-down cards when it is your turn, turn your face-up pile over to make a new face-down pile and turn the top card. If you have no cards at all you are out. Last player with cards wins. If a player shouts Snap in error, that player's face-up pile is put in the centre as a snap pool; if the top of any pile later matches the top of a snap pool, the first to call Snap pool takes both piles.
keyRules: Deal entire deck equally face-down; players do not look at cards.
Turn top card face-up on your turn; turn the card facing away from yourself so others see it first.
When two face-up pile tops match in rank, any player may shout Snap; first to do so wins both piles.
False snap: your face-up pile is moved to the centre as a snap pool.
When a pile top matches a snap pool top, first to call Snap pool wins both.
No face-down cards on your turn: turn your face-up pile over and continue; no cards at all means you are out.

strategy.basic: Keep eyes on ALL piles, not just your own. Memorize what is on top of each pile. Be ready to shout.
strategy.intermediate: Peripheral Vision: Watch the hands flipping cards, not just the cards. Anticipate.
strategy.advanced: Voice Projection: A loud, clear 'SNAP!' overrides a mumbled one in a tie.
tips: Don't cover the card with your hand while flipping.
Remove face cards for younger children to simplify.

variations.name: Single Pile
variations.description: Players turn cards onto a single central pile. When two consecutive cards match, any player may call Snap and the first to do so wins the centre pile. A player who calls Snap incorrectly gives the top card of their pile to the player who turned the card. Simultaneous calls create a snap pool; first to call Snap pool when the centre matches a pool wins the pool.
variations.emptyOverridesReason: Single-pile is a rule variant only; no engine constant overrides documented in sources.

variations.name: Simultaneous calls
variations.description: If two or more players shout Snap at the same time, the matching piles are combined into a snap pool in the centre. If two or more call Snap pool simultaneously, the matching player pile is added to that pool. Some groups use an object in the centre to grab; the hand underneath on the object decides who was first.
variations.emptyOverridesReason: Simultaneous-calls describes snap pool rules only; no engine overrides needed.
